It builds the science and AI behind our platform, from job analysis and assessments to AI interviews and predicting performance. Led by our Head of Science, Aiden Loe, and working closely with our COO, Paul-Louis Caylar, the team brings together business psychologists, psychometricians and AI scientists. Together, they make sure every hiring decision on our platform is accurate, consistent and fair. As Maki grows, the Science and AI team’s job is to show, with evidence, that our approach leads to better hiring decisions. About the Role The AI Applied Scientist turns our science into results for clients. The rest goes on improving the scoring systems that every client relies on. 1. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Agent Eval Platform
jobs.jd: The Role Moveworks' AI agents don't just generate text — they act. They plan, call tools, and change real state in enterprise systems on behalf of 5.5 million employees. Building agents is no longer the bottleneck. Improving them is: knowing whether a change made the agent better, why a conversation failed, and which part of the system should be fixed. You'll build the loop that makes our agents improve themselves — finding failures in real use, deciding which part of the agent harness is responsible, checking every proposed fix on cases the fixer never saw, and turning each fixed failure into a permanent test. We improve the system around the model: instructions, tool descriptions, routing, knowledge and memory. We don't train the model itself. The work is blend of ML and systems engineering. You'll decide whether a signal is trustworthy enough to act on, and build the infrastructure that produces that signal reproducibly across hundreds of customer organizations. This isn't a model-training role, and it isn't a testing role. It's applied ML at a point where the methodology genuinely isn't settled: LLMs judging LLMs is an open research problem, and we're working it against agents that take real, irreversible actions in stateful, multi-tenant enterprise environments. What you get to do in this role: Judge design and calibration A shared base judge with per-item rubrics expressed as configuration next to the dataset — so eval authors express intent, rather than forking a prompt per eval Splitting the problem correctly: deterministic validators for checkable world state ("was the ticket created, with the right item, routed to the right approver?"), and an LLM judge for the parts that are genuinely fuzzy — was the clarifying question appropriate, was policy followed, was the path efficient Scoring that reports its own confidence , so uncertain judgements route to a human instead of quietly becoming trusted signal A standing calibration loop against human-labeled trajectories, run in partnership with our annotation team — they own the human labeling, you own the calibrated judge artifact. How consistently humans agree with each other sets the ceiling on how good any judge can be, so raising that ceiling is part of the job Guarding against correlated blind spots: our user simulator and our judge are both LLMs, and they can be wrong in the same direction Offline↔online divergence: when simulation and production disagree, being the person who can say why, and keeping the suite re-seeded from new production failures so it can't quietly overfit Self-improving agent harness This is where the pillar is headed, and a large part of why the seat exists. You'll build the components that let the agent harness get better from its own use, without changing the model underneath. Finding what to improve: surfacing where the agent falls short in real use, including failures that look like success Synthetic data and environments: generating scenarios and the seeded enterprise worlds they run in — with expected outcomes and checks — from real failures or ahead of what customers ask for, and making sure what gets generated is realistic, hard enough, and doesn't leak the answer Deciding where a fix belongs: understanding why the agent failed and which part of the harness should change: its instructions, tools, routing, knowledge or memory Proposing improvements: optimizing those components against simulation rather than against production traffic Checking before anything ships: verifying every proposed change on cases it wasn't tuned on, catching regressions an average would hide, and keeping the part that proposes a change separate from the part that judges it Evals that grow: every fixed failure becomes a permanent test, so the suite gets stronger the more the agent is used Safe across many customers: learnings stay scoped to one organization where they must, and admins approve anything org-specific The infrastructure that runs it: a loop that runs reproducibly, at scale, across hundreds of customer organizations The guardrail that keeps it honest: end-state outcomes are what we hold the agent to To be successful in this role you have: 2+ years in applied ML, data science, or ML-adjacent engineering, with a track record of work that shipped and got used Experience turning subjective human judgement into a measurement that holds up — one that other people, and ideally other models, can act on. This is the core of the job Strong applied ML fundamentals, and comfort treating LLMs as a component you evaluate, prompt, and fine-tune rather than one you pretrain Strong Python, and the discipline to ship production-grade code rather than notebooks Ability to think and communicate clearly about complex problems — a large part of this job is convincing engineers that a number means what you say it means, and being right A high degree of ownership and a bias toward shipping at startup pace Comfort with ambiguity, and the judgement to know when a measurement is good enough to act on Experience in at least 3 of these: LLM-as-judge or automated evaluation design, and calibrating it against human judgement Human annotation programs: rubric authoring, label quality, and annotator throughput as a real constraint Search ranking, recsys, or online experimentation evaluation — golden-set staleness, offline/online divergence, side-by-side rater agreement. This is the closest existing analog to agentic eval, and it transfers directly Fine-tuning and evaluating small models: SFT, preference tuning, distillation Reward modeling, RLHF/RLAIF, or process reward models Agent trajectory analysis and step-level fault attribution Prompt engineering as an engineering discipline — versioned, tested, and measured, not tuned by vibes For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $161,300 - $274,200, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. jobs.jd: The Role We're building the runtime infrastructure that powers Moveworks' AI agents — the systems that orchestrate, execute, and deliver agent responses to millions of enterprise users in real time. This role sits where large language models meet distributed systems. You'll apply machine learning, LLM, and distributed systems expertise to make agents plan, reason, and use tools reliably, and you'll build the production systems that run those agents at enterprise scale. Our AI agents can plan, execute multi-step workflows, call tools, wait on human input, and resume — all while maintaining correctness, observability, and low latency. The systems that make this possible are what you'll build and own. What you get to do in this role: Agent orchestration engine — A state machine that manages long-running agent sessions, coordinating planning, execution, and user interaction across multiple LLM calls and tool invocations Model routing and adaptation — Choose, route between, and fine-tune or distill LLMs for specific agent tasks. Meet enterprise requirements such as granular permissions, data freshness, explainability, and preserving general knowledge. Distributed session management — Lease-based ownership using conditional writes, heartbeat protocols, and crash recovery via checkpointing Event-driven message pipeline — FIFO queues for ordered delivery, consumers for event processing, and real-time streaming via gRPC and Socket.IO Structured concurrency — Running multiple concurrent tasks per session with fail-fast semantics and graceful cancellation Observability infrastructure — OpenTelemetry instrumentation, distributed trace context propagation across async boundaries, custom span lifecycle management for sessions that span minutes Caching and state layers — Redis, DynamoDB KV stores with per-org/per-bot scoping, batch read optimization, and hot-reload configuration Tool and agent connectivity for LLMs: Build MCP and agent-to-agent (A2A) capabilities, including tool discovery, namespacing, and tool selection over large tool catalogs, so the LLM picks and calls the right tool from thousands of candidates. Token efficiency and context engineering — Lower the agent's cost and latency through prompt and context discipline, caching, speculative and parallel model-call scheduling, and reducing tokens spent across multi-step LLM reasoning chains. Open-weights model adoption and evaluation — Quickly stand up newly released open-weights LLMs at different quantization levels, run them in a test environment, and benchmark their accuracy, latency and cost on agent tasks. Use the results to decide which models reach production. To be successful in this role you have: You should have deep experience in at least 3 of these areas: Distributed systems: consistency models, idempotency, exactly-once delivery, distributed locking/leasing Concurrent/async programming: Python asyncio, Go goroutines, structured concurrency, cancellation handling Event-driven architectures: message queues (SQS, Kafka), pub/sub, backpressure, delivery guarantees Database systems for infrastructure: DynamoDB (conditional writes, transactions), Redis (connection pooling, pub/sub) Observability: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, span context propagation, Prometheus metrics gRPC/protobuf: streaming RPCs, service interface design, error handling patterns Machine learning: Large language models, natural language processing, LLM evaluation Required: 5+ years building production backend/infrastructure systems Strong in Python or Go (ideally both) Experience designing and operating systems that handle real traffic at scale Hands-on experience building production systems that use LLMs or other ML models Comfort with ambiguity — these are novel problems without textbook solutions Relevant past experience: Building and shipping products on large language models with techniques such as RAG, chain-of-thought, self-reflection, tool and function calling, and agentic reasoning. Improving relevance or quality through careful experimentation: designing metrics, building evaluation datasets, and developing new features and signals for ranking or model selection. Research or applied work in machine learning, LLMs, agentic systems, information retrieval, or ranking and relevance. Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. Your work will span model internals, quantization and model compression, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, inference engines, serving architecture, and benchmarking to improve latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, and cost per token while preserving quality and reliability.

You will work with kernel and platform engineers to investigate serving problems, compare configurations, and resolve performance and quality regressions. You will evaluate model- and engine-level optimizations together with distributed inference designs, including request routing, scheduling, prefill/decode coordination, and multi-node GPU execution. Your improvements will be validated through reproducible benchmarks and safe production rollouts under real-world workloads.

  • Own optimization projects for specific model families, customer endpoints, or serving backends.

  • Produce design documents, performance reports, rollout plans, and customer-facing technical explanations.

Must-haves

  • Strong engineering skills in Python and PyTorch.

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Data Science organisation sits at the heart of Deliveroo powering decision-making across our 3 sided marketplace.

Our Analytics community is highly active, with guest lecturers, study groups, mentorship programmes and a robust technical review process.

Our data scientists come from all kinds of backgrounds but have excellence in common.

We’re looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our London team (working hybrid, 3 days in the office). In this role, you’ll enable high-quality human-led decision-making to maximise impact.

 

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Senior Data Scientist at Deliveroo, your goal is to maximise business impact within one of our product areas. A core part of the role is designing, running and interpreting experiments, and using causal inference to guide product decisions in complex, real-world settings.

You will go beyond simply answering “did this feature work?” and instead focus on understanding what the true impact is, why it worked or did not work, and how results generalise across users, markets and time.

Here’s what your day-to-day might look like:

  • Driving Strategy/insights through Experimentation: Leading the design of both simple and complex experiments and proactively translating findings into strategic direction.

  • Master Causal Inference: Apply advanced techniques to estimate long-term and heterogeneous treatment effects.

  • Drawing reliable conclusions in settings with selection bias or imperfect randomisation.

  • Drive Deep Product Insights: Uncover the fundamental drivers of experiment performance, determining why features succeed and how results generalise across different users, markets, and timeframes.

  • Using insights from past experiments to improve future decision-making.

What You’ll Need to Thrive

  • Strong experience designing, running and interpreting A/B experiments in production environments

  • Solid understanding of causal inference concepts

  • Ability to apply statistical thinking to messy, real-world product problems, not just ideal experimental setups

  • Great communication skills in person, in writing and in code, with both technical and non-technical audiences

  • A problem solver with a deep analytical mindset

  • Ability to think creatively and insightfully about business problems

  • Familiarity with SQL

  • Excellent people skills as you will be meeting with stakeholders to translate business needs into data science problems

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you’ll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that’s constantly evolving. We’re food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day.

🌱 See your impact, fast Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment.

🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support.

🌎 A culture built for builders High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.

​​💰 Share in the success you help create Competitive salary and equity options, so you’re rewarded for the impact you make.

 

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Find more about how we hire here.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you’ll have the opportunity to let us know once you’ve submitted your application. We’ll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

You will validate your work experimentally on state-of-the-art robotic platforms — removing bottlenecks to deployment and enabling robots to safely operate around humans. You will work with the inventor of CBFs, as well as top scientists and engineers at Amazon developing the next generation of safe autonomy. As a Prime Video team member, you’ll have end-to-end ownership of the product, user experience, design, and technology required to deliver state-of-the-art experiences for our customers. You’ll get to work on projects that are fast-paced, challenging, and varied. You’ll also be able to experiment with new possibilities, take risks, and collaborate with remarkable people. We’ll look for you to bring your diverse perspectives, ideas, and skill-sets to make Prime Video even better for our customers. With global opportunities for talented technologists, you can decide where a career Prime Video Tech takes you! Key job responsibilities The science challenges include: - Heterogeneous customer responses. The same customer responds differently to ads depending on what they’re watching, how engaged they are, and their broader streaming context. We need to understand and predict this variation to make better advertising decisions in real time. - Signal sparsity in streaming. Unlike search or retail advertising, streaming offers no clicks, no conversions, and limited direct feedback. We must develop creative approaches to infer customer preferences, intent, and tolerance from indirect behavioral signals. - Personalization at scale. A one-size-fits-all ad experience leaves value on the table for both customers and the business. We build systems that adapt ad load, placement, and content to individual viewers across 100M+ customers and 100k+ titles. - Small effects, large variance. Ad interventions typically produce 0.1-2% shifts in engagement, effects easily overwhelmed by natural behavioral variance. Measuring, attributing, and optimizing these small signals requires rigorous experimental design and causal methodologies. - Competing objectives. Revenue, customer engagement, long-term retention, and advertiser value are in tension. We develop principled frameworks to navigate these tradeoffs and optimize for sustainable outcomes rather than any single metric.
